- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to reflect bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model consistently underestimates sharp upward moves (e.g., spikes > 5% from prior day) — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for such events.  
- Model overestimates downward moves after spikes — cap downward corrections at 3–5% below prior peak to avoid excessive sell-off.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model often fails to correct — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast to counteract.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days — adjust forecast to be 1–2% higher than historical 30d average of recent 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model tends to be flat — introduce 0.5–1% upward drift to avoid underestimating volatility.
